root_cause.text: The microchip-core-qspi driver relied on hardware-automatic chip select control, which kept the built-in CS line low whenever the transmit buffer was written to, causing it to interfere with GPIO-controlled chip selects on other devices attached to the same controller.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "if there are two devices attached to this QSPI controller that the in-built chip select is set low while linux tries to access the device attached to the GPIO." The patch resolves this by switching from automatic hardware CS control to software-controlled CS management via the `DIRECT_ACCESS_EN_SSEL` register bit, implementing explicit `set_cs()` and `setup()` callbacks that allow the driver to control when the built-in CS is active, and only activating it during actual transfers to the built-in device rather than leaving it asserted continuously.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add symbolic macro definitions for QSPI Direct Access register bit fields to improve code clarity and maintainability.
intent_record.what: Added a new comment block and three macro definitions for QSPI Direct Access register control: DIRECT_ACCESS_EN_SSEL (BIT 0), DIRECT_ACCESS_OP_SSEL (BIT 1), and DIRECT_ACCESS_OP_SSEL_SHIFT (value 1), inserted between STATUS_MASK and BYTESUPPER_MASK definitions.
intent_record.how: These new macros provide symbolic constants for controlling QSPI direct access mode via slave select (SSEL) signals. They enable code to manipulate QSPI hardware registers using named bit positions and shift values instead of magic numbers, improving code readability and maintainability when accessing QSPI direct access functionality.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add chip select control and initialization functions to properly manage active-low SPI device chip select states during setup and runtime operations.
intent_record.what: Added two new static functions to the mchp_coreqspi driver: mchp_coreqspi_set_cs() which controls the chip select line by manipulating the DIRECT_ACCESS_OP_SSEL register bits, and mchp_coreqspi_setup() which initializes active-low chip select devices to their inactive state during probe by setting the DIRECT_ACCESS_OP_SSEL bit.
intent_record.how: These functions enable proper chip select management for SPI devices. mchp_coreqspi_set_cs() provides runtime control of the CS line state (active/inactive), while mchp_coreqspi_setup() ensures active-low CS devices start in the correct inactive state during initialization. This prevents undefined CS behavior and ensures correct SPI communication with devices that use active-low chip select signaling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused static function `mchp_coreqspi_setup_op()` to eliminate dead code.
intent_record.what: Removed the static function `mchp_coreqspi_setup_op()` which read the control register, set CONTROL_MASTER and CONTROL_ENABLE flags, cleared CONTROL_CLKIDLE, wrote back to the register, and returned 0.
intent_record.how: This function is no longer called anywhere in the codebase after this change. Removing it eliminates dead code and reduces the driver's code footprint. The control register initialization that this function performed must now be handled elsewhere or is no longer necessary for correct operation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure chip select is explicitly asserted before executing SPI memory operations to prevent transmission errors from unselected devices.
intent_record.what: Added a call to `mchp_coreqspi_set_cs(mem->spi, true)` after `mchp_coreqspi_config_op(qspi, op)` and before the opcode transmission check in the `mchp_coreqspi_exec_op` function.
intent_record.how: This change explicitly sets the chip select (CS) line to active (true) at the beginning of SPI operation execution, ensuring the slave device is selected before any command transmission occurs. This prevents potential race conditions or undefined behavior where CS might not be properly asserted before data transfer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure chip select is properly deasserted on all error paths to prevent leaving the SPI device in an inconsistent state.
intent_record.what: Added a call to `mchp_coreqspi_set_cs(mem->spi, false)` in the error handling path before the mutex_unlock() call in the mchp_coreqspi_exec_op function.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that the chip select (CS) line is deasserted (set to false/inactive) whenever the function exits via the error label, regardless of which error condition was encountered. Previously, CS could remain asserted if an error occurred, potentially leaving the SPI device in an inconsistent state. Now the CS is properly cleaned up before releasing the operation lock.

intent_record.intent_summary: Declare missing local variables required by subsequent code additions in the probe function.
intent_record.what: Added two new local variable declarations `u32 num_cs, val;` to the mchp_coreqspi_probe function's variable declaration section.
intent_record.how: This change introduces two unsigned 32-bit integer variables that will be used later in the probe function to store values (likely the number of chip selects and a temporary configuration value). Without these declarations, subsequent code that uses these variables would fail to compile.

intent_record.intent_summary: Configure chip select count from device tree and remove custom setup callback to fix CS handling in the Microchip CoreQSPI driver.
intent_record.what: Added code to read 'num-cs' device tree property with fallback to 1, set ctlr->num_chipselect accordingly, added explanatory comment, and removed the line assigning mchp_coreqspi_setup_op to ctlr->setup.
intent_record.how: The change enables dynamic configuration of chip select count from device tree while providing a sensible default of 1 for single CS operation. Removing the setup callback assignment allows the SPI core to use its default setup handler instead of the driver-specific one, potentially fixing issues with CS handling or setup operations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Enable software-controlled chip select mode and implement proper QSPI controller initialization instead of relying on a static chip select count.
intent_record.what: Replaced hardcoded `ctlr->num_chipselect = 2;` with two function pointer assignments (`ctlr->setup` and `ctlr->set_cs`), added hardware initialization code that enables the QSPI controller in master mode and configures chip select into software-controlled mode via register writes.
intent_record.how: This change shifts chip select handling from a static count to dynamic software control via callback functions. The hardware initialization enables the QSPI master controller and switches the chip select mechanism from hardware to software mode, allowing more flexible CS management during runtime. The `use_gpio_descriptors = true` setting now works in conjunction with the software-controlled CS mode.

commit 8596124c4c1bc7561454cee0463c16eca70b5d25
Author: Naga Sureshkumar Relli <nagasuresh.relli@microchip.com>
Date:   Mon Aug 8 12:16:02 2022 +0530

    spi: microchip-core-qspi: Add support for microchip fpga qspi controllers
    
    Add a driver for Microchip FPGA QSPI controllers. This driver also
    supports "hard" QSPI controllers on Polarfire SoC.
    
    Signed-off-by: Naga Sureshkumar Relli <nagasuresh.relli@microchip.com>
    Reviewed-by: Conor Dooley <conor.dooley@microchip.com>
bic_trace_step.reason: This is the initial commit introducing the microchip-core-qspi driver. The vulnerability root cause is that the driver relies on hardware-automatic chip select control without providing a way to disable it. Examining the code: (1) In `mchp_coreqspi_setup_op()` at line 310-314, the driver sets `CONTROL_MASTER | CONTROL_ENABLE` but never disables automatic CS control. (2) In `mchp_coreqspi_write_op()` at lines 226-245, every write to the TX data registers (REG_TX_DATA and REG_X4_TX_DATA) causes the hardware to automatically keep CS low, which interferes with GPIO-controlled chip selects on other devices. (3) There is no mechanism to disable the built-in CS line or to control it manually. The driver lacks any CS control configuration (e.g., no CS disable bit being set in CONTROL register, no manual CS handling). This is a bug-introducing commit because it introduces the vulnerable construct (relying on automatic CS control without disabling it) and does not contain the fix (which would involve disabling automatic CS or providing manual CS control).
